concrete_capability_transition: CLI JSON output and implicit exit handling change from mixed raw runtime envelopes and partial projections into stable bounded public JSON projections plus deterministic exit semantics across existing commands.

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Makes every existing JSON-capable Brownie CLI command return a stable bounded success or error contract with explicit exit semantics so a headless caller can branch safely without parsing raw runtime internals.
Projects task-list progress and route-candidate data into capped JSON structures with truncation metadata while preserving runtime ownership of progress computation and next-action policy.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development and progress_visualization by making CLI output dependable for machine callers and bounded for human/operators without moving runtime authority into the CLI.
answers.new_capability: A caller can use brownie --json status, inspect task, inspect run, list tasks, mode list, run, and resume with a common ok/command/exit_code envelope and command-specific bounded projections.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before CLI-7, run/resume had bounded projections but status, inspect, list tasks, and mode list exposed runtime-shaped envelopes; list tasks JSON could include raw progress_overview and route internals, and exit-code classes were not covered as a public contract.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: CLI-9 and CLI-10 would have to assert ad hoc human output or raw runtime schemas, making headless automation fragile and leaking internal authority details into the public CLI contract.
answers.non_duplicative: CLI-5.1 fixed invocation identity and scoped resume correctness, and CLI-6 added human progress/mode UX. CLI-7 changes the machine-facing output and exit contract for existing commands, which those phases deliberately left open.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase uses existing runtime.status, task.inspect, run.inspect, task.list, mode.list, headless.run.drive, and headless.continue_once calls.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It adds executable CLI projections and behavior tests, not a readiness, report, digest, verdict, history, or summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust runtime authority and protocol methods remain unchanged; user-visible CLI behavior changes by emitting stable public JSON and deterministic exit classes.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can branch on stable exit codes and bounded JSON rather than reimplementing runtime policy or depending on raw protocol details.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the CLI-7 Product DoD gap and leaves CLI-8 packaging/help, CLI-9 arbitrary-repository Golden Journey, and CLI-10 restart/recovery Golden Journey as the remaining required gaps.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: CLI-7 updates the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm the PR changes executable CLI JSON and exit behavior without weakening the phase-value guard or adding wrapper-only surfaces.

exit_criteria: All existing JSON-capable CLI commands return a stable success envelope with ok=true, command, exit_code=0, and one command-specific payload key.
brownie --json status, inspect task, inspect run, list tasks, and mode list use bounded CLI public projections instead of raw runtime result envelopes.
brownie --json list tasks caps task rows, progress groups, blocked groups, and headless route candidates and includes deterministic truncation metadata without route reasons.
brownie --json run and brownie --json resume retain their bounded CLI projections and include the common success envelope.

Invalid invocation, runtime unavailable, runtime timeout, runtime communication failure, invalid runtime response, and runtime JSON-RPC error use deterministic exit classes and JSON error codes without raw payload or path leakage.
No new runtime RPC, generic passthrough, report, readiness, history, digest, verdict, summary, CLI-owned policy, or CLI-owned workspace mutation authority is added.
behavior_evidence: brownie-cli test behavior verifies stable JSON success projections for status, inspect task, inspect run, list tasks, mode list, run, and resume.
brownie-cli test behavior verifies deterministic exit codes for invalid invocation, runtime unavailable, timeout, invalid response, and runtime JSON-RPC error.
brownie-cli test behavior verifies large task-list JSON caps and truncation metadata.
brownie-cli test behavior verifies route reasons, runtime paths, environment values, and raw internal payloads are not exposed.
real runtime smoke tests continue covering status, list tasks, mode list, run, and resume through the CLI/runtime process boundary.

closes: CLI-7 Human / JSON Output and Exit Codes

accepted_capability: Existing CLI commands now expose stable bounded public JSON projections with a common success envelope.
CLI errors retain bounded messages and deterministic exit classes suitable for headless callers.
behavior_evidence: Fake runtime test behavior covers command-specific JSON projections, large progress bounds, truncation metadata, exit codes, and raw-data suppression.
Existing real runtime smoke tests continue to exercise the CLI/runtime process boundary.
safety_boundary: No Core Runtime terminal campaign state is reopened or mutated.
No new runtime JSON-RPC method is added.
The CLI does not read ledgers, discover Mode Packs from files, evaluate permissions, select tasks, apply patches, or own recovery policy.
JSON and human output remain bounded and exclude raw prompts, provider responses, file content, stdout/stderr payloads, commands, environment values, paths, and secrets.
non_goals: No arbitrary-repository golden journey or restart/recovery golden journey closure.
No Mode Pack, Product DoD, provider, permission, workspace mutation, replay, or fail-closed semantic redesign.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected a generic JSON-RPC passthrough because it would expose runtime internals as CLI API.
Rejected unbounded list task JSON because it would make headless output unstable and risk internal leakage.
Rejected CLI-side task or mode-policy interpretation because the Rust runtime owns that authority.
Rejected packaging and Golden Journey work because CLI-8 through CLI-10 own those separate Product DoD gaps.
technical_debt: CLI-8 must define practical installation, packaging, and command help.
CLI-9 must validate the arbitrary-repository golden journey.
CLI-10 must validate restart/recovery including scoped resume and runtime-owned recovery provenance.
next_capability_rationale: After CLI-7 lands, proceed to CLI-8 Installation / Packaging / Help rather than adding another output wrapper.
